note: Long runs heard as groups of four: the nine-note run, the scale up the octave four notes per beat with the metronome, the same run in groups of four, then the book's octave run. The old Stage selector of tempos and Key selector are now moves (any key, 60 to 90 bpm), every tool written at 60, with the tempo and the line about another key as params; each block has its feel to reach and each run step states its range and the semitone climb.

exercise.title: Nine notes and the octave
exercise.why: A long run is short groups joined together, so hearing it in fours keeps every note in its place when the tempo goes up.

cells.text:
Press Play below to hear the run: two chords set the key, and the mic starts with them. The run goes from Do up to Re above the high Do and back down, and each pass starts a semitone higher, the last one reaching the top of your range. Sing it on "ah", and close towards "oo" at the top.
If a pass smears, listen to it and come in on the next one.

Press Start exercise below: the metronome and the mic start together, at {{=bpm}}. Sing up the scale from the low {{1}}, four notes per beat, and hold the high {{1}} when you reach it. Breathe, then run back down the same way and hold the low {{1}}. Sing it on "ah".
Practice until {{4}} and {{7}} are as clear as the notes around them.
{{?bpm}}At a faster tempo the top of the run goes flat first, so listen there.

Press Start exercise below: the metronome and the mic start together. Sing the run in groups of four, one group per beat: {{1}}, {{2}}, {{3}}, {{4}}, then {{2}}, {{3}}, {{4}}, {{5}}, each group starting one note higher, up to the high {{1}}. Sing it on "ah".
Practice until each group starts on the click.
{{?key}}In another key the notes are new, but every group is still four steps up.

Press Play below to hear the run: the mic starts with it. The run goes from Do up to the high Do and back, four notes per beat, and each pass starts a semitone higher, the last one reaching the top of your range. Sing it on "ah", and hear it in groups of four.
Practice until each group of four lands on its beat.
